name: K-Board Pro 4
summary: Dedicated family entry preserved for future editor routing and firmware mapping.

notes: Under WinMM the device enumerates as a single "K-Board Pro 4" port pair; under WMS the same physical device splits into two separately-named endpoints, "K-Board Pro 4 Control Surface" and "K-Board Pro 4 Expander" (see the named_application profile below). Purpose of the Expander endpoint is unconfirmed.

Central's bootloader replies to a standard Universal Device Inquiry with a real Identity Reply. Central's application firmware detects the same inquiry but replies with a KMI-proprietary "editor message" instead (SYX_FIRMWARE_VERSION_MSG), carrying no manufacturer/product/family ID fields - sendsysex parses this format separately to populate the same bootloader/application version fields.
Applied automatically to both the Peripheral and Central sends, regardless of --midi-backend.

Central's application-mode SysEx relay (and its bootloader's page-format parser) recognizes a valid message header within the first ~24 bytes and immediately starts a blocking operation (an I2C flash-erase on the peripheral MCU it's relaying to, or the bootloader's own erase) before it can accept more USB data. A small first window clears the host fast enough to avoid landing mid-blocking-op; a long first-gap delay then gives the device time to finish before the next window, after which the transfer proceeds at the steady-state chunk delay. The extended post-delay gives the bootloader/relay time to finish writing/verifying and reboot before the port closes.
Requests a reboot into bootloader mode for K-Board Pro 4.
targetState is incorrect on this superseded entry; do not use.

No "role" field on this entry (unlike firmware_1_2_2_0_peripheral below) - deliberate: it keeps this the family's role-less/primary firmware target, which --fw-update KBP4's bootloader-flash step resolves to by default. Do not add a role here or add another role-less firmware entry; payload resolution becomes ambiguous.
Central firmware payload. Adds I2C_LOCK_BOOTLOADER: Central auto-locks its own and all 4 peripherals' bootloaders once it detects a fully-assembled 4-peripheral unit.

Single monolithic SysEx message - a flat 512-byte-page flash image, not Hex_to_SysEx's chunked format. The bootloader's payload parser only understands the page format and cannot parse a chunked file at all.

Do not repackage this into multiple separately-framed SysEx messages: the bootloader's packet_data_init() calls erase_app() unconditionally on every validated message header with no once-per-transfer guard, so a second top-level message re-erases the app region and destroys whatever the first message just wrote. Only sendsysex's single-message sub-split path (slicing the one message's bytes into smaller transport writes, inserting no new SysEx framing) is safe here.

role="peripheral" excludes this entry from --fw-update KBP4's generic bootloader-flash step (which resolves the role-less/primary payload). Instead it's sent explicitly, first, while Central is still in application mode, before the bootloader-entry -> bootloader -> Central-firmware-flash -> reboot sequence. There is no independent version check against the device for this payload (peripherals have no MIDI identity of their own), so it is resent unconditionally whenever the Central version check decides an update is due. If the device is already sitting in Central's bootloader (e.g. resuming an interrupted run), this payload is sent as a catch-up step after Central's flash completes and the device reboots back to application mode, since it can't be sent while Central is in bootloader mode.

targetState is application, not bootloader: the peripheral's own bootloader has no SysEx/MIDI parser at all and is only reachable over I2C. This payload is sent to the Central APPLICATION port while Central is running its normal app firmware. Central's app then puts all 4 peripherals into their own bootloaders over I2C, erases them, and relays this same page-formatted payload to each one.
Same single-monolithic-message / page-format constraints as firmware_1_2_2_0_central apply here too.

Safe to re-send if a transfer is interrupted; the Central relay re-erases the peripheral's flash on every attempt. Re-sending requires the Central device to be back in its normal application-mode port first, since this payload's targetState is application.
Matches WinMM's port naming (device enumerates as a single "K-Board Pro 4" port pair). See the named_application profile below for WMS's split-endpoint naming of the same physical device.

Matches WMS's port naming ("K-Board Pro 4 Control Surface" / "K-Board Pro 4 Expander") for the same physical device WinMM enumerates as a single port pair. Shares role "main" with the WinMM application profile above so automatic-update port selection works regardless of which backend's naming matched.
